messages:
incident-bot: [PAGER] SEV2 — NewtonCorp (VPC eu-west-1): KV/prefix cache hit-rate dropped 78% in last 3m. Error rate increased. Paging oncall: @maria (oncall).

maria (oncall): on it. seeing alerts in console. pulling metrics now.

kevin_r: I can help, started an initial query against the kv-stats stream. preliminary: prefix misses spiked, lots of new tenant prefixes from NewtonCorp.

aj: NewtonCorp dedicated pool (pool-neo-12) seeing sustained high eviction churn. possible prefix pollution from a batch job?

jules_sre: tagging — this looks like cache pollution (many writes with new prefixes). Customer impact: elevated latencies for generate endpoints (+160ms p50) and increased 500s for some calls (~6% of requests).

ops-bot: CPU on pool-neo-12 GPUs at 74%, io wait unhealthy. Autoscaler not kicking due to reserved capacity cap.

maria (oncall): timeline: will isolate NewtonCorp traffic to a quarantine route to stop new prefixes from entering shared cache. Kevin, can you confirm a safe prefix filter?

kevin_r: yes — we can add a routing rule: `if tenant_id == "newtoncorp" then route->isolated-pool` and disable prefix prefetch for that pool. Also suggest `kv:ttl=30s` for the quarantine pool to avoid long-term pollution.

sophia-l: adding the rule now to routing config. patch:```yaml
- route: tenant:newtoncorp
  pool: isolated-neo-12
  kv_prefix_cache: disabled
  kv_ttl: 30s
```

aj: live patch applied. routing change rolled to 3 nodes. verifying traffic shift…

ops-bot: Route update propagated. 92% of NewtonCorp requests now hitting isolated-neo-12.

jules_sre: checking hit-rate on shared pool: prefix hit-rate recovering from 4.2% -> 51% in 2m. error-rate dropping.

maria (oncall): good. next step — mitigate already-polluted entries in shared pool: plan A run targeted eviction for prefixes matching `newton:*` and reduce kv shard TTLs for 10m. any objections?

kevin_r: go ahead with targeted evictions. command: `redis-cli --scan --pattern "newton:*" | xargs redis-cli del` (we'll run against in-memory kv mirrors with safety flag dry-run first).

aj: executed dry-run, ~32k keys matched. switching to live delete in 30s.

ops-bot: delete job started, rate-limited to 2000 deletes/s. monitoring evict queue.

jules_sre: after 3m of deletes, shared prefix hit-rate at 78%, request 500s down to baseline (0.6%), p50 latency back to +25ms. impact window reduced.

maria (oncall): notifying NewtonCorp via CA rep: minimal customer-facing errors, degraded latency for some long-running batch jobs; they may see spike in their retry logs. sending status note. @sophia-l please prepare postmortem checklist.

sophia-l: will do. initial RCA notes: suspect a misconfigured backfill job from NewtonCorp that started emitting a high cardinality set of prefixes (new session ids) into cached writes. follow-ups: policy to limit per-tenant prefix injection, automated detection for prefix cardinality spikes, docs for customers on backfill best-practices.

maria (oncall): final status: NewtonCorp traffic isolated, shared pool healthy, eviction completed. continuing 1h watch. marking incident as mitigated — will create incident ticket and assign follow-up tasks to SRE and Product. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident mitigated by oncall team. Escalation timeline and actions recorded in ticket INC-2312-NEWTON.

sophia-l: post-incident actions created: 1) per-tenant prefix quota enforcement (P1), 2) telemetry alert for prefix-cardinality > 10k/min (P2), 3) client guidance doc for safe backfills (P3). assigning owners.

kevin_r: exporting metrics and logs to s3 for deeper forensics. path: `s3://redwood-incidents/2312005555-newton/`

maria (oncall): thanks team — switching back to regular oncall. tagging for retro.

aj: thumbs. :thumbsup:
